Audi has halted all imports to the U.S. and is holding incoming inventory at port in response to new tariffs. While vehicles imported before the tariffs will keep prior pricing, future imports are expected to reflect added costs through increased destination fees.

### Pricing impact

Audi has announced price increases for most of its 2026 models, ranging from $800 to $4,100. The largest increases will affect premium models, including the A8 and RS 7.

### Production impact [...] Porsche has not announced any official response to the tariffs. The German carmaker shipped additional inventory into the U.S. ahead of the tariffs taken effect, and will honor prices for orders made in March.

### Pricing impact

Porsche confirmed a 1.2%–2.9% price increase for the new year. Orders delivered before January 5th are exempt from the adjustment.

### Production impact

No changes to production or import plans have been announced at this time.

### Manufacturer response [...] Tesla has expressed concerns about the impact of the recent 25% U.S. tariffs on imported vehicles and auto parts. In a letter dated March 11, 2025, Tesla informed the Trump administration that these tariffs could increase production costs for vehicles manufactured in the U.S. The company emphasized its efforts to localize the supply chain but acknowledged continued reliance on global parts sourcing.

  #### Five decisions that separate resilient EV supply chains from vulnerable ones [...] Tariffs on Canada and Mexico have been complicated, to say the least. With the USMCA up for review next year, the expectation is that tariff-reducing concessions could be made during negotiations. However, at the beginning of August, the US raised tariffs on Canada to 35%, keeping tariffs of 25% on Mexico. For both countries, USMCA-qualifying automotive parts are exempt from tariffs temporarily, while vehicles that are USMCA-compliant are currently tariffed at 25%. Cars built in the US and [...] Now, a 50% tariff rate applies to stamped components such as bodyshop panels, brackets and structural elements, even if they would otherwise qualify as car parts, meaning the rate goes up from 27.5% (25% for USMCA compliance) to 50%.

The new scope also targets product codes for derivatives and products made from the materials, including the likes of paints and sprays, which are often used in the automotive supply chain.

### How Will Tariffs Impact the Prices of Cars?

Prices for new cars could increase by as much as $6,000 per vehicle on models under $40,000. This significant hike is due to the added cost of importing vehicles and parts, which manufacturers will likely pass on to consumers. As a result, both new and used car markets will be affected, with potential ripple effects on financing and insurance costs.
